**Finding resubmitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

The repair was to the finding's rationale, not the document. The verifier's own analysis confirmed the substance was right, so the only defect worth curing was that my rationale did not pre-empt the failed deterministic check. The resubmitted finding now:

- **Names the artifact explicitly** — "audit frequency limited" fails because there is no audit clause for frequency, notice, or cost limits to attach to. A regex miss against a non-existent clause is not evidence of a defect.
- **Adds § 1 (p0007) to the cited paragraphs**, since the only access-related provision in the agreement runs in our favor (Contractor must comply with Clear Capital's system access and security policies) and is affirmative support for the no-system-access element of the preferred position.
- **States the direction of the obligation** — under § 3(b) substantiation flows from RadialSpark to us, and billing is time-and-materials, so there is no usage metric or underpayment exposure a vendor audit could police.

Zero edits remains the correct minimal action. Absence of any audit right binding us is at least as protective as the preferred position, and opening this point would invite RadialSpark to negotiate *for* an audit right it does not currently have — a net loss even if we won every parameter.

As noted before and still outside this rule's scope: § 3(b) permits unilateral rate changes on 30 days' notice, and any *customer-side* audit right over the Contractor's time-and-materials records would need to be raised under a separate pricing or records-retention playbook item.
